title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: Self-RAG and Corrective RAG (CRAG)
summary: Self-RAG (Asai et al., 2023) adds self-reflection tokens to RAG: the LLM learns to generate special tokens like [Retrieve] (should I retrieve at all?), [Relevant] (is this retrieved doc relevant?), [Supported] (is my answer grounded?), and…

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body:
**Self-RAG** (Asai et al., 2023) adds self-reflection tokens to RAG: the LLM learns to generate special tokens like `[Retrieve]` (should I retrieve at all?), `[Relevant]` (is this retrieved doc relevant?), `[Supported]` (is my answer grounded?), and `[Utility]` (is this answer useful?). This allows the model to actively decide whether retrieval is needed, whether retrieved docs are useful, and whether the generated answer is faithful — all within a single model. Standard RAG always retrieves and blindly trusts the output.

**CRAG (Corrective RAG)** (Yan et al., 2024) adds a retrieval quality evaluator that scores retrieved documents. If all retrieved docs are "wrong" (low relevance score), CRAG triggers web search to find better documents before generation. CRAG introduces: (1) a lightweight relevance evaluator; (2) a "query decomposition for web search" step for when local retrieval fails; (3) knowledge refinement (strip irrelevant portions of retrieved docs).

diagrams.title: Self-RAG and Corrective RAG
diagrams.explain: **Self-RAG** lets the model decide *whether* to retrieve and critique its own output. **CRAG** grades retrieved chunks and takes a corrective action — refine the query or fall back to web search — when they are wrong. Both trade extra LLM calls for fewer confident wrong answers; always cap the loops.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
ADVANCED RAG ARCHITECTURE COMPARISON
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

NAIVE RAG:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query → Retrieve → Generate → Answer

SELF-RAG:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query → [Retrieve?] 
           │ YES           │ NO
           ▼               ▼
        Retrieve         Generate directly
           │
           ▼ [Relevant?] for each doc
        Filter docs
           │
           ▼
        Generate → [Supported?] → if NO: re-generate
                   [Utility?]  → if LOW: re-retrieve

CRAG:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query → Retrieve top-5
           │
           ▼ Relevance Grader
        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
        │ All docs irrelevant (score<0.5) → Web Search → Generate
        │ Some relevant               → Filter + Generate
        │ All relevant                → Standard Generate
        └──────────────────────────────┘

AGENTIC RAG (LangGraph):
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Query 
  │
  ▼
AGENT (LLM)
  │ tool_call: retrieve_documents
  ▼
TOOL: Vector Search
  │ result
  ▼
AGENT (LLM)
  │ tool_call: run_sql_query (needs more data)
  ▼
TOOL: SQL
  │ result
  ▼
AGENT (LLM)
  │ tool_call: calculate
  ▼
TOOL: Calculator
  │ result
  ▼
AGENT (LLM)
  │ final answer (no more tool calls)
  ▼
Answer

GRAPH RAG:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Corpus → Entity Extraction → Knowledge Graph

At query time:
Query → Entity Detection ("CEO of Company X")
     │
     ▼ Graph traversal
CEO_X → [works_for] → Company_X
      ← [cited_in] ← Earnings_Call_2023
                   → [mentions] → Paper_Y
                                → [authored_by] → Author_Z

Answer: "Author Z wrote the paper, which CEO of Company X cited"
→ Multi-hop in < 1 second via graph traversal ✓

MULTI-HOP ITERATIVE RETRIEVAL:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Q: "What is the refund policy for items purchased during the summer sale?"

Hop 1: Q: "What was the summer sale?"
       → Retrieved: "Summer sale ran June 1 - Aug 31, 2024"
       A: "Items purchased June 1 - Aug 31, 2024"

Hop 2: Q: "What is the refund policy for purchases made June-August 2024?"
       → Retrieved: "Sale items: 30-day return window, store credit only"
       A: "30-day return, store credit"

FINAL: "Items from the summer sale (June-August 2024) have a 30-day 
        return window, with refunds issued as store credit only."
```

options: Multi-query is more powerful (explores different semantic directions) but 3-5× more expensive.

Formula: RRF_score(doc) = Σ 1/(k + rank_i) where k=60 (empirical constant, prevents top-ranked docs from dominating) and rank_i is the document's rank in the i-th result list.
Standard RAG always retrieves, always uses all retrieved docs, and never evaluates retrieval quality.
quiz.explanation: Standard RAG always retrieves, always uses all retrieved docs, and never evaluates retrieval quality. Self-RAG adds self-reflection at every step via special tokens — the model decides when to retrieve, evaluates each retrieved doc's relevance, and checks its own answer for faithfulness.

quiz.explanation: Fusion RAG generates multiple queries (4-5 variations) for a single user query, retrieves results for each, applies RRF to fuse the ranked lists, then generates the answer. RAG Fusion (Raudaschl 2023) showed this approach improves answer quality by 30% over standard RAG. Key advantage: multiple query perspectives uncover different relevant documents.

quiz.explanation: FLARE generates answer tokens one sentence at a time. When the model is about to generate a sentence with low-confidence tokens (probability < threshold), it triggers retrieval using the partial sentence as a query, then continues generation using the retrieved context. Retrieval happens exactly when the model needs it, not just at the start.
